comments.text: Hey Cory! I wanna drop this lil tidbit in the hopes it brings you some comfort! <3 when I was studying Marine Biology, I learned that sharks do not see humans as food and hardly even enjoy the taste of humans to begin with. Majority of shark attacks stem from them mistaking us for one of their preferred foods, a very prominent example of this being when we are surfing. When we lie on our stomach on surfboards, splay our arms out to the sides and wade through the water, from the sharks view below us looking up at our silhouettes we look to them like wounded seals ~ it might be going out on a limb too, but you should look up (if you're unfamiliar with em!) nudibrachs ~ there are so many awesome different varieties including Glaucus (sea dragon!), ones that look like sheep covered in green leaves and bunnies lol ~ Sea Angels, Sea Butterflies, Blue Buttons, Little Sail/Sea Raft, and pointed-nose Chimaera(Ghost Shark that looks like Frankenweenie lol)! Those are some of my favorite creatures in the sea and maybe knowing these lil fellas exist down there too might make you feel a  bit better about the ocean!! :)

comments.text:
For those who don't know or haven't played this game: 

"Sharks and minnows" is a game a lot of swimming athletes play where one swimmer is chosen to be the shark. The other swimmers have to complete a lap to the otherside of the pool without being tagged/eaten by the shark. If you get tagged, you become another hostile swimmer that has to help the original shark to tag as many swimmers as possible. The last one to survive wins essentially. The game was made to get your adrenaline pumping and motivate swimmers to push their limits and be faster.

This video game takes the original game to the next level by putting you in a "real" situation by making you swim in the dark, and avoid as many other creatures and making you a lone swimmer.

comments.text: Hey Cory, my mom is a diver and studied marine biology plus zoology and behaviour in sharks. Sharks generally don’t just attack out of nowhere. If they do it could be that you missed a “warning” they gave you, warnings from sharks could be their gills standing out, fins down to their side and swimming sharper (sharp turns/looking frustrated) my mom regularly sees small sharks while diving and they don’t mind her at all! In fact my mom is more worried about seals than she is the sharks. Unfortunately there’s a bad case of rabies in seals where I’m from so she’s had to be extra careful. The fish my mom dives with often greet her and clean her goggles/gear. Despite what people say fish are actually super intelligent like all other animals and do infact have emotions and feelings. I also have thalasaphobia so I completely get why you’re scared haha. Many sharks will accidentally attack divers if they feel like they’re being put in a bad situation or if they feel threatened. Sharks are VERY curious and will often follow divers around to watch them and check them out. Sharks also enjoy nibbling on divers! It’s actually quite cute. They nibble for the same reasons that puppies nibble on you when they’re young, it’s all just curiosity/interest. Sharks often make friends with divers and recognise divers that they like. They also protect divers from other sharks/fish. Personally I’m terrified of dolphins! Those are animals I do NOT want to mess with. Something that may help you with your fear is going on professional dives to see small sharks in a controlled area! If anybody is interested in going diving, PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE! Make sure you pick the right diving course to follow! Many places don’t know what they’re doing and end up injuring the animals or the divers themselves. My mom dives/teaches diving with professional divers. They work with conservationists and actually care about the animals they work with. Last fun fact that will hopefully cheer you up, there’s a shark called the “shy shark” and when they get a fright/scared, they curl into a ball and cover their face with their tail!
